name: Australian Premium Solar (India) Limited
summary: Solar-module, rooftop and pump growth has become substantial, but weak cash conversion and materially inconsistent annual reporting prevent a reliable quality or attractiveness ranking. sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text: APS is a policy-sensitive solar-module, rooftop and pump growth business, not yet an evidence-backed compounder. Capacity reached 1.2 GW after the October 13 commissioning, and signed FY26 sales grew 61.3%. The decisive risk is that growth absorbed cash while the later annual report printed a materially inconsistent cash-flow table. At the October 19 close of ₹224.05, the signed earnings multiple is only 7.81×, but an apparently inexpensive multiple does not resolve accounting reliability. Full conditional funding and valuation diagnostics are provided; all three aggregate scores remain NS because material financial inputs are Low confidence and G2 is on hold. A reconciled filing and verified collection/funding bridge, not another capacity announcement, would change this assessment. [S3,S4,S8,M1]

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Research cutoff: 20 October 2026, India reporting dates; latest completed NSE session October 19 because October 20 is a market holiday. Australian Premium Solar (India) Limited, APS, INE0P0001010, NSE Emerge; listing began January 18, 2024. Verified issued shares 20.16 million imply market capitalization ₹451.6848 crore. Consolidated AS accounts under section 133 are used; the older standalone series is separately identified. Horizon is five investor years, nominal INR before personal taxes, with a 15% assumed equity hurdle and illustrative ₹5 lakh liquidity reference. G1/G3/G4 are Conditional; G2 is Hold. Confidence is Medium on identity, sales and observed commissioning, but Low on financial reconciliation, cash realization and valuation inputs. [S3,S7,S8,M1]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Canonical factors: GOV 4, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 6, EXEC 6; CAP, CASH, BAL and EARN are NS pending reconciliation. IAS R/D/P are also NS on the same material input limitation; L is 5. The factor and score audits retain exact original weights, missing-factor coverage and mathematical bounds without renormalizing. Diagnostic factor illustrations are not final scores. No governance failure is inferred from a filing defect or commercial RPT. No persistent-cash numeric override substitutes a number for NS: FY25 CFO was positive and the scale/perimeter changed, although the cumulative cash shortfall is economically important. [S3,S8,S9,R1]

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text: APS sells manufactured solar modules and implements rooftop and agricultural pump systems, with inverter distribution and installation/service activities. The Gujarat plant supplies both external customers and internal project requirements; internal module consumption must not be added again to consolidated revenue. The FY23 prospectus mix was 67.71% modules, 28.51% rooftop installation and 3.77% pumps. Management describes more than ₹300 crore pump revenue in FY26 and a 90–120 day collection cycle. That is a different mix from the old module-heavy business. Group companies include APS Rooftop Solar, APS Solar Pump, APS Renewable Energy and Aplus Solar Cell; remaining 49% of Aplus was acquired on June 26 for ₹99,990. Despite its name, Aplus is not evidence of a commissioned upstream cell factory. Management explicitly deferred cell manufacturing and discussed BESS instead. [S5,S6,S8,S9]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: The useful business advantages are a manufacturing-plus-installation channel, local service experience and domestic qualification access. A durable pricing moat is not established: management prices modules frequently, generally does not hold more than two months of module orders, and says additional scale need not raise margins materially. FY23 top-ten customers represented 44.65% of sales and top-ten suppliers 72.51% of purchases; current concentration is not disclosed with equivalent detail. The peer set separates Solex module/EPC economics, Premier integrated cell/module economics, Waaree Renewable EPC projects and Websol cell exposure. None is a direct substitute for APS, and their margins or market multiples are not imported into the valuation. Crisil’s dated rationale attributes part of the FY25 margin step-up to falling input prices, a contrary fact to a purely structural-margin thesis. [S6,S9,R1,P1–P4]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Revenue was ₹74.1624/98.1213/94.5592/149.6729/438.8773/707.9571 crore for FY21–26, with restated standalone scope through FY23, annual standalone FY24 and group FY25–26. The growth audit shows both five- and three-year reported CAGRs and every annual rupee addition; they are not represented as pure organic volume growth. Parent FY26 sales ₹688.9525 crore versus ₹432.8030 crore also grew about 59.2%, so subsidiary consolidation alone does not explain expansion. Signed H2 sales ₹405.4864 crore versus ₹275.1255 crore rose 47.4%, while PAT ₹29.2642 crore versus ₹27.0120 crore grew only 8.3%. H1/H2 comparisons show ongoing but decelerating sales expansion and much weaker incremental profit conversion. REV 8 reflects sustained scaling, not management’s 30–35% forecast; the Medium/history ceiling prevents a 9. [S3,S7–S9]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The accessible runway combines the commissioned additional 400 MW line, pump awards and rooftop execution, but it is not the entire national solar TAM. May’s award covers 5,000 pumps for more than approximately ₹100 crore. June’s Bihar award covers 16 MW under CAPEX-plus-RESCO terms, describing ₹68 crore in the first year and approximately ₹9 crore annually for ten years. These amounts are not summed into immediate revenue or risk-free recurring profit; timing, collection and maintenance economics require contract execution. Central diagnostic growth of 20% is below management guidance but still demanding: terminal annual run-rate revenue approaches ₹1,959 crore. It requires additional fixed capital and working capital beyond the current 1.2 GW footprint. The model funds each rupee rather than assuming nameplate capacity alone creates cash. BESS is optional and separately stress-tested at ₹20 crore with no immediate revenue credit. [S4,S6,S12,S13]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Promoters/group declared 14,639,342 shares, 72.62% of issued capital, at March 31 and no new direct or indirect encumbrance during FY26. This is not proof of no pre-existing encumbrance or an October holding. FY26 public preference shares and promoter warrant conversion raised the share count by 420,000; the annual report says ₹18.18 crore was deployed into capex ₹5 crore, WC ₹12 crore and general purposes ₹1.18 crore. No proceeds are added again to forecast cash. Related purchases from Abwatt were ₹35.9064 crore, about 6.8% of gross raw-material purchases, and promoter rent/other expense ₹0.8823 crore. The whole-time director’s remuneration was 4.43× median employee pay with no reported increase; an exact five-year pay series was not located. Aplus minority acquisition was interested-promoter and issuer-described arm’s length, not independently valued. Delivery is mixed: the May presentation expected the next module line by August; actual start was October 13. The unmodified audit opinion does not cure the table contradictions. [S5,S6,S8,S14]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text: The coherent signed May 22 results, refiled July 9, reconcile opening cash ₹30.2139 crore plus CFO −₹5.064 crore, CFI −₹45.3537 crore and CFF ₹54.7015 crore to closing ₹34.4977 crore. FY25 CFO was ₹24.4004 crore; two-year CFO/PAT is 0.197 and post-fixed-capex cash is negative ₹41.5134 crore. Receivables/advances absorbed ₹128.4167 crore in FY26, partly funded by liabilities, not by cash capex itself. Later annual CFO ₹68.681 crore and its net-cash bridge are internally inconsistent. July’s reply addressed diluted-EPS XBRL/legibility and cannot have corrected the later annual table. Debt differences now reconcile mainly as ₹7.5962 crore shifted current, with total debt essentially unchanged; trade asset/liability increases nearly offset in net WC. Annual other expenses differ by ₹0.2038 crore, while the closing equity difference is only about ₹0.0021 crore; this remains unexplained. Annual cash notes identify ₹15.2164 crore FDR and current provisions identify tax ₹20.4918 crore. Annual group ageing reports ₹61.9019 crore beyond six months, unlike the much smaller older-balance share in standalone ageing; reconciliation is needed before treating either as a reliable collection forecast. [S3,S7,S8,S10]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: The linked 67-month model starts from March claims, estimates the seven-month bridge, then measures five investor years. Bear/central/bull assume revenue growth −5%/20%/30%, economic EBIT margins 6%/11%/12.5% and terminal EV/EBIT 5×/8×/10×. Bear also slows working capital and absorbs a 10% opening receivable loss. Central retains bank fees and normalizes below FY26 economic margin rather than capitalizing the entire input-price benefit. Term debt amortizes, taxes and remaining line payments consume cash, new credit is explicitly uncommitted, and rescue shares issue at half the dated price if required. Diagnostic IRRs are -17.6%/29.0%/52.1%. These are conditional arithmetic, not targets or final R scores. The reverse-growth solution, 27-cell margin/growth/multiple grid, ±3-point hurdles and FDR/tax/debt/capex/credit sensitivities are retained. Market P/E and book value are cross-checks only. [S3,S8,R1,M1]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The most important failure variable is conversion of pump/project receivables into usable cash. Lower module prices or input inflation can reduce margin at the same time as public-project collection slows; bank guarantees, tax payments, supplier finance and scheduled debt then compete for liquidity. The bear diagnostic produces about a 62% terminal price loss even without a modeled survival failure. A more severe stress combines −10% growth, 4% margin, 4× exit, 15-point higher WC and a 10% opening receivable loss. No-new-credit and demand-recall cases explicitly show dilution rather than assuming rescue lenders. G2 is an additional information risk: the range may be understated if the financial statements contain larger errors than the identified differences. Government-linked demand does not eliminate credit, timing or warranty risk. [S3,S6,S8,R1]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: A five-year 5× price requires approximately 38.0% annualized return and 10× requires 58.5%, before personal taxes. Central diagnostic value is around 3.6× the dated quote; the aggressive bull exceeds 5× but remains below 10× and requires 30% annual sales growth, sustained 12.5% economic margin, substantial reinvestment and 10× terminal EBIT. The historical preference price ₹433 is not an intrinsic-value anchor. Given unreliable reporting inputs and cash-intensive growth, 5× is possible only under demanding assumptions and 10× is speculative, not a supported compounder forecast. [S8,M1]

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Monitor the accounting reconciliation first, then aged receivables and actual collections, economic margin, commissioned-line utilization, remaining payments, tax settlement, deposit access, order service obligations, fresh dilution and tradability. The structured monitoring plan states company-specific baselines and distinguishes investigation alerts from thesis breaks. Management’s May claim of approximately ₹50 crore post-year-end collections is not credited as a separate cash inflow because forecast WC already governs cash realization and no reconciled cash statement verifies it. Forecast bridge values are never labelled current bank balances. [S3,S6,S8]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Hold — unresolved financial reliability. The research is a completed conditional review, not a favorable investment classification and not an allegation of misconduct. A low quoted earnings multiple and an attractive modeled central return cannot override G2 or Low material financial confidence. No trade or allocation recommendation follows from the illustrative ₹5 lakh exit exercise. Reopen scores when a reliable annual-to-signed bridge, cash restriction/collection evidence and operating-margin normalization support the relevant factors; future uncertainty alone is not a reason to force NS. [S3,S8]

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary sources include the final IPO prospectus, FY24/FY25/FY26 annual reports, May/July signed results, May call/presentation, June acquisition, pump and Bihar awards, March promoter declaration, October commissioning, dated Crisil rationale and four distinct peer disclosures. All arithmetic is in crore rupees except explicitly identified source units. Open questions are the annual cash/profit/ageing reconciliation, exact remaining module-line and hybrid-project investment, bank deposit accessibility, current facility headroom, and current customer/supplier concentration. The older Crisil analysis combines only APS and rooftop subsidiary and is not a current all-group solvency clearance. Model assumptions and sensitivities are disclosed separately from reported facts; probability calibration is not required for a conditional scenario model. [S3–S15,R1,P1–P4]

funding_assumptions: Opening term ₹34.5368 crore includes ₹7.5962 crore current maturities; repay those during year one and the remaining balance over months 13–48, consistent with dated rating maturities no later than March 2030 but not an exact bank amortization schedule.

Seven-month opening bridge requires unverified financing; it is not presented as October observed cash or borrowing. Investor share count starts from verified 20.16 million and hypothetical rescue dilution begins only after the quote.

Remaining commissioned-line payment ₹10 crore is a 0–20 crore assumption. Historical ₹45.8556 crore capex and historical preferential proceeds are not recredited. BESS ₹20 crore is a separate no-extra-revenue sensitivity, not approved capacity.

Maintenance capex equals depreciation as an estimate; incremental revenue requires additional fixed-capital investment at sales/capital turnover 3/4/5 plus operating working capital. Actual engineering budget is not represented as known.

opening_claim_audit.included_once: Trade payables, customer advances/deposits, statutory dues and audit/other current provisions are netted in opening and projected operating WC. Gratuity policy exists but no separate noncurrent employee balance is disclosed; employee/expense amounts are not silently omitted from the current-provision aggregate.
opening_claim_audit.tax: Full ₹20.49182043 crore opening tax provision paid during first 12 months. ₹5.11725117 crore authority balances excluded from operating WC, no base cash recovery or duplicate tax offset; recovery sensitivity separately shown.
opening_claim_audit.FDR: ₹15.216401947 crore excluded from freely available opening cash and terminal equity; accessibility/release sensitivities bound this conservative assumption. No evidence all deposits are permanently restricted is asserted.
opening_claim_audit.legacy: ₹4.7292 crore deferred-tax reserve deducted once at exit; reserve-release sensitivity. No verified separate noncurrent employee/other claim on the group balance sheet.
opening_claim_audit.minority: June 26 acquisition of remaining 49% Aplus costs ₹0.009999 crore cash; other three subsidiaries 99.99% held. Terminal 0.01% minority reserve is approximate, with 1% sensitivity.
opening_claim_audit.historical_equity: FY26 share and warrant proceeds are already in March balances and current shares. No duplicate IPO/preference cash added.
opening_claim_audit.leases: AS accounts expense rent; operating EBIT assumptions retain occupancy cost. No separate finance-lease debt was identified in the reviewed consolidated borrowings; no unsupported lease liability or lease cash credit is invented.

GOV.reason: Disclosed minority acquisition, public preference issue and related dealings are not established abuse; repeated material reporting defects and unverified commercial fairness limit stewardship.

MOAT.reason: Manufacturing and installation channels offer useful access; short-price horizons, imported cells, contestable capacity and raw-material windfalls weaken evidence of durable pricing advantage.

REV.reason: Both reported five-year and three-year enterprise growth exceed 30%; parent growth near group growth and two comparable half-years support real scaling. Pump mix, prices and changing perimeter limit organic attribution; Medium/history ceiling 8, not TAM credit or a single-quarter adjustment.

DUR.reason: Commissioned 1.2 GW and actual pump/rooftop awards provide accessible demand; subsidy/program dependence, service obligations and cash needs constrain duration.

CAP.reason: Economic incremental proxy exceeds assumed hurdle after retaining bank fees and excluding FDR from cash; one expanding group period, ageing and unresolved annual profit/cash differences prevent a reliable final return score.

CASH.reason: Signed two-year CFO/PAT 0.197 and post-capex cash deficit are usable adverse diagnostics; positive FY25 and ongoing expansion are contrary context. Later annual CF and ageing cannot be reconciled sufficiently for a final factor.

BAL.reason: Gross debt classification now reconciles and ample earnings are reported; FD availability, receivable quality and conditional credit access materially affect survival stress, so no forced medium score.

EXEC.reason: Sales and first/additional TOPCon capacity delivered, but the next line missed the May August target and cash conversion lagged. BESS/cell plans are not scored as delivered.

EARN.reason: Operating sales dominate reported growth but H2 PAT growth sharply trails sales, input-price benefits complicate persistence and annual profit differs from signed results without a bridge.

R.reason: A fully funded conditional central return is calculated; material accounting/asset-realization confidence, not absent probabilities, blocks a reliable expected-return factor.

D.reason: Bear and severe loss/funding paths are explicit; uncertain receivable ageing and cash reliability prevent a final downside factor.

P.reason: Reverse required growth and entry sensitivities are solved; apparent low earnings multiple could reflect accounting and collection risk, so price-implied optimism cannot be reliably scored.

L.reason: 60/60 observed sessions and ₹36.31 lakh median turnover give 2.75 days at 5% for ₹5 lakh, a starting 7. Downgrade to 5 for fewer-than-100-PAN and high-price-variation cautions plus unknown depth; generic SME alert alone does not imply inactivity.

diagnostic_scoring.status: No canonical financial score assigned from diagnostic arithmetic. Refer to the explicit valuation scenarios and capital-return proxy; they are not ranking inputs.
